memory_update.text: NVDA, TSM, MU, AMAT, and AMKR form a compact US-listed universe for the AI accelerator + HBM + advanced-packaging stack: product leader, foundry/CoWoS owner, HBM supplier, equipment supplier, and OSAT/advanced-packaging supplier.

The node is better modeled as a multi-variable capacity chokepoint: logic wafer starts, HBM stack supply, substrate availability, packaging throughput, yield learning, and customer qualification all determine final AI accelerator output.

Strong adjacent candidates not included due to the 5-candidate limit include AMD, AVGO, ASML, LRCX, KLAC, INTC, SNPS, CDNS, ASX, and BE Semiconductor/ASMI if non-US primary listings are allowed. These should be revisited in later Layer 1B passes by sub-node.

SK hynix and Samsung are critical HBM suppliers but are not clean US-listed common-stock candidates; they should be tracked as external private/foreign supply-chain evidence rather than primary US-listed candidates unless ADR/OTC eligibility is explicitly allowed.

Add MU as a direct US-listed HBM candidate for the AI accelerator/HBM/advanced-packaging node; highest evidence strength among new US-listed names due to specific NVIDIA and AMD platform announcements.
Add AMKR and ASX as OSAT/advanced-packaging capacity candidates; both need deeper verification of exposure to flagship HBM-attached AI accelerators versus broader advanced-packaging markets.
Add AMAT and KLAC as upstream equipment/process-control candidates tied to HBM, 2.5D/3D packaging, IC substrates, and yield learning rather than direct accelerator unit shipments.

For this node, distinguish direct chokepoint suppliers from second-order enablers: direct = HBM vendors and advanced-packaging/test capacity; second-order = tools, inspection/metrology, materials, substrates, and yield-learning systems.

Still need a follow-up pass on US-listed or US-accessible substrate/material names, thermal-interface materials, test-equipment vendors, EDA/IP, and smaller specialty tool suppliers; some may be below $1B or non-US-listed.
Add AMKR as a direct OSAT/advanced-packaging capacity candidate for the AI accelerator HBM packaging stack; watch Arizona and Korea expansion, advanced-packaging revenue, and customer concentration.
Add ASX as a US-listed ADR for ASE Technology, a large OSAT with explicit HBM/chiplet/AI advanced-packaging positioning.
Add ONTO as a high-priority inspection/metrology candidate tied to HBM4 ramp and advanced AI packaging yield control.
Add CAMT as a high-priority inspection/metrology candidate with direct HBM, chiplet, hybrid bonding, and OSAT/HBM customer order evidence.
Add FORM as a probe-card/test candidate for HBM known-good-die and advanced-package test requirements.

Direct HBM vendor exposure remains a separate coverage gap for this node. Micron Technology is US-listed and should be evaluated in a dedicated HBM-memory pass alongside non-US HBM leaders SK hynix and Samsung, but was not included here because this pass emphasized second-order suppliers and the candidate list was capped at five.
The most underappreciated public-market mappings in this node may be yield-enabling tools and back-end capacity, not only GPU designers or front-end wafer equipment.

node: AI accelerators, HBM memory, and advanced packaging stack
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the US-listed universe around the AI accelerator + HBM + advanced-packaging capacity node. The strongest direct exposures are the AI accelerator product leader, the leading foundry/CoWoS capacity owner, the US-listed HBM memory supplier, and equipment/OSAT suppliers tied to HBM and advanced packaging ramps. This pass intentionally limits candidates to 5 and does not rank them as buy/sell ideas. Expanded the universe around the HBM plus advanced-packaging chokepoint. The highest-relevance US-listed additions are not only accelerator designers, but HBM suppliers, OSAT/advanced-packaging capacity providers, and packaging/process-control equipment vendors. Micron is the most direct US-listed HBM exposure; Amkor and ASE add outsourced advanced-packaging/test capacity exposure; Applied Materials and KLA are second-order equipment/process-control suppliers tied to HBM, 2.5D/3D packaging, IC substrates, yield learning, and capacity ramps. These are research candidates only, not trading recommendations. Expanded the US-listed universe around the HBM plus advanced-packaging constraint with emphasis on less-obvious second-order beneficiaries. The strongest mapped candidates are OSAT capacity providers and inspection/metrology/test vendors whose tools or services are needed as AI accelerators move to HBM, chiplets, 2.5D/3D integration, hybrid bonding, and higher bump/interconnect density. This is a research universe, not a buy/sell list.
